title: Hexagon binning (H3 or custom hexagons) with statistics
question: Can an AI agent turn points into a hexagon map, in 2D or 3D, that I can share?
answer: Yes. A map-v1 analysis step runs the hexbin operation in the viewer's browser when the link opens: points are summarised in H3 cells (or Turf hexagons of a chosen side) by count, density per km², or the sum, mean, min or max of a numeric field. The result is a coloured, optionally 3D layer. Polygon data becomes points first with the random-points step (the dot-density recipe), chained with { "step": 0 }.
triggers: Make a hexagon map of these points
Bin these incidents into H3 hexagons and extrude them in 3D
Make a population hexagon map from census blocks
inputTypes: Point GeoJSON or CSV with coordinates
Points made by an earlier random-points step

required.name: source
required.description: A point layer, or { "step": n } for an earlier step's points.

optional.name: method
optional.description: h3 (default; resolution 0-15, 7 is about 5 km², 8 about 0.74 km², 9 about 0.1 km²) or turf with cellKm (hexagon side).

optional.name: statistic
optional.description: count (default), density (points per km² of each cell's own area), or sum, mean, min, max of a numeric field.

optional.name: field
optional.description: Numeric field for sum, mean, min and max. Blank and non-numeric values are skipped and reported; a cell with no numbers gets null, not 0.

optional.name: extrude
optional.description: true raises cells by the statistic (MapLibre 3D).

optional.name: keepEmpty
optional.description: true keeps cells with no points (count 0) across the data or study area.

optional.name: overlay
optional.description: A polygon layer as the study area: whole cells that touch it are kept, never clipped.

optional.name: area
optional.description: "view" reads only features in the current map view; use with a camera for layers beyond the limit.

steps.action: Read llms.txt, this recipe and api/capabilities.json; note the engine and execution environment you actually have.
Read the source metadata: geometry type, field names and types, spatial reference, extent, sentinels and query support. Query real values before filtering; never invent fields.

Confirm point geometry and the feature count. Pick a resolution from the area (about 1,000 to 20,000 cells reads well) and a statistic; check that the field is numeric. Up to 100,000 points are read: filter with where (or use area "view" with a camera) when the layer has more, and say so.
Add { "operation": "hexbin", "input": 0, "options": {...} } to analysis and validate the spec; unknown options and bad inputs are reported.
Return the #map=json: link; the browser bins the points when it opens. In a running page, analysis.run("hexbin", { input, options }) does the same and returns a summary and binning metadata.
Open the link: the hexagon layer is listed with a choropleth on the statistic, and the summary does not start with "Incomplete:". Report skipped points and an incomplete read if either appears.
Return the link. Results are recomputed for each viewer; the link carries the steps, not the cells.

artifact.structure: map-v1 with a point layer (or a random-points step) and an analysis step { operation: "hexbin" }.

outputs.format: Hexagon GeoJSON layer in the page (h3_id or cell_id, point_count, cell_area_km2, density_km2, field statistics, complete)

verification: Summary has no "Incomplete:" or the gap is reported
limitations: Reads up to 100,000 points; MapLibre holds at most 50,000 features of a big ArcGIS layer, so filter it or use area "view".
Points only: lines and polygons are not split by area; turn polygons with a count into points with random-points first.
Cells are recomputed in each viewer's browser; nothing is stored on a server.
3D cells need the MapLibre engine; ArcGIS 2D colours them flat.
recovery: "Too many cells": lower the resolution, use a larger cellKm, drop keepEmpty or narrow the area.
"Incomplete:" in the summary: add a where filter or area "view" with a closer camera.
"needs a numeric field": choose a numeric field or use count or density.

examples.title: Ventura County population in 3D hexagons
examples.prompt: Make a 3D hexagon map of Ventura County's population from the 2020 census blocks.

dataset.label: California Census 2020 Redistricting Blocks (Esri, U.S. Census Bureau)

checks: Opened on MapLibre: 7,843 blocks loaded, 42,232 dots (hidden) and 1,408 H3 resolution 8 cells drawn in 3D with a legend; no console errors.
The same link with ?tutorial=hex-population starts a seven-step tutorial.
